I've been farming this same land for forty years. My father farmed it before me. At my age, I don't experiment much — I do what works, what I know, what my body can still manage. Some of my grandchildren help during busy periods, but mostly I handle it myself and my wife helps with the lighter work. My son sends money from the city, but I keep farming because I know nothing else and I don't want to depend on him entirely.

My land is 3.1 mu. Every mu grows wheat in winter, then maize right after harvest. That's how I've always done it. Same land, two crops a year.

**Wheat:** I'll plant in mid-October like always. I buy seed from the township supply station — the improved variety they recommend, not the expensive new ones. I keep some seed from last year too, but I mix it. Before planting, I'll rotary-till the field after maize harvest and apply base fertilizer — compound fertilizer bag plus extra urea. At jointing I'll top-dress more urea. I'll irrigate at sowing if soil is dry, again at jointing, again at heading. Three times usually, maybe four if spring is dry. I'll spray herbicide once in spring and watch for rust — if I see it I spray fungicide. I expect around 450 jin per mu, maybe more if rain is good.

**Maize:** Right after wheat harvest in June I plant maize directly without plowing — no energy for that in the summer heat and we need to get seed in fast. I use hybrid seed, the kind from the seed shop that everyone around here uses. I apply base fertilizer at planting and chase with urea when plants are knee-high. Summer rains help so I irrigate maybe twice — once if soil is too dry after planting, once at silking if it doesn't rain. I spray for corn borer once, maybe herbicide once early. I expect around 550 jin per mu.

My body is not as strong as it was. I keep things simple. I don't try new methods I haven't seen work with my own eyes.
